name: Can an accessible bathroom remodel be done in an existing slab home?

mainEntity.name: How do contractors create a curbless accessible shower in a Los Angeles slab foundation home without causing drainage problems?
mainEntity.text: How do contractors create a curbless accessible shower in a Los Angeles slab foundation home without causing drainage problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: A slab foundation does not automatically rule out an accessible bathroom remodel, but it can make a curbless shower more complex. Contractors often need to recess part of the floor, adjust plumbing, and build a properly sloped waterproofed shower pan. If the slab is post-tensioned, heavily reinforced, or too shallow for safe modification, a full zero-entry shower may not be practical. In that case, a low-threshold shower can still improve accessibility substantially while reducing structural risk. The drainage plan matters as much as the threshold height, because a poorly designed curbless shower can leak or leave standing water outside the enclosure. Homeowners in Los Angeles should ask whether the slab can be cut, where the drain will sit, and how the waterproofing will transition into the main bathroom floor before demolition begins.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but the floor must usually be recessed, the drain relocated or carefully positioned, and the waterproofing system designed around the slab conditions. If the slab cannot be altered enough, a very low-threshold shower may be a better solution than forcing a full zero-entry build.
